summary: Target 28e9 has the complete original 1280x720 fourteen-frame matrix with 28 passing ordinary/export draw audits, two actual new vehicle studio views, and one continuous native drive from Weave via Crosstown to the existing lower Foundry entrance. The route arrived and stopped, saved 22848 physical steps and exported the original record; compound-contact samples and external journal gaps are retained. Trusted short X, pause/input release, conditional high-altitude pitch/G recovery, research lifecycle and downloads were actually observed on 81926 with bounded source-inheritance evidence. Both ground WE1 full-pitch/recovery cases remain failed, severe-step trajectories remain unconverged, and hardware performance, upper-route travel and finite-supply native flight remain unverified. This is final assembled local evidence, not universal functional acceptance or public deployment.
scope: Final local evidence aggregation for target runtime 28e9bc41. Assembly rereads original evidence and hashes; it does not rerun tests, physics or browsers, and performs no remote operations.

New 28e9 evidence includes the original-resolution fourteen-frame matrix, two actual current vehicle studio views and one continuous native city drive to the lower Foundry entrance, with original conditions, source guards and explicit limitations.

Native controls and research/UI were actually captured on 81926b47. Target applicability is a separately documented implementation-inheritance inference: 170/172 sources unchanged, with the production physics and ordinary-scene blocks unchanged. Original PNGs, downloads, timestamps and build IDs remain 81926.

X trigger timing, application routing, action-local motion, global quaternion travel, finite/bench supply, observation windows and physical outcomes remain separate. Both ground-start WE1 full-pitch/recovery failures remain failures.
ANGLE SwiftShader is actual WebGL software-GPU execution. It does not establish user-hardware FPS, keyboard rollover, human handling, universal latency or routes beyond the observed lower entrance.
Numerical contact and finite-recovery records clarify remaining boundaries. They are not counted as native route, pixel or hardware certification.

Route arrival, complete stored physical-step inputs, 20 Hz state curves, sparse contact telemetry and external automation journals have separate coverage. Observed compound contacts and missing returned journal lines are not removed or relabelled.

openGates.summary: 25 samples have positive final-slice compound contacts; 26 have any positive internal microstep. The body includes wheel bump-stop cylinders and chassis boxes. Read-only saved-pose geometry supports front-wheel hard-stop/ground contact as an inference; actual contact pair/shape, point, force, impulse and continuous duration were not captured. This route is not certified compound-contact-free or shell-impact-free.

All 1130 requested native driving events match application receipts and original record values. Eight external returned lines are absent; the collector reports 1245 telemetry observations but the original journal contains 1244 lines. No missing timestamps or observations were fabricated.

The continuous Weave-Crosstown route reached the existing lower Foundry entrance and stopped within the original 8 m arrival radius. Upper ascent, maintenance court, the transverse z=-100 crossing and full drive-flight challenge are not validated by this run.
Both native ground-start groups stop near 196 degrees and finish inverted, wheel support 0, rigid contact count 4 and G limited. High-altitude bench success does not pass these cases.

90 km/h / 10 cm complete trajectories remain sensitive through 60-1920 Hz. Lower contact equation depths or SAT peaks do not imply complete convergence; the old single-wheel step-only SAT was smaller even though its all-solid maximum was larger.

Native X and high-altitude WE1 use 350 bar bench external supply. Numerical early recovery cancels the original task and uses zero external supply; neither certifies arbitrary finite-supply maneuvers.
Actual application rejection and product visible-state implementation are verified. The original 08 menu PNG does not independently display the refusal text.
Final 7.0333 sim seconds of the climb are sparse observations. The later high-altitude pitch/recovery has contiguous zero-contact samples, with an explicit 0.4917 sim-second W-only marked-head gap.
Software WebGL pixels do not establish user GPU FPS, driver behavior, hardware keyboard rollover or human handling feel.

Dark high facades, clipped lamps, repeated distant building forms, weak material cues on the flat road fitting and simplified nose/interior remain. Two new vehicle views do not recapture all older views.

Controls retains one unspecified resource 404, UI two unspecified resource 404s, and route one unspecified resource 404; matrix and vehicle diagnostics preserve their observed URLs when available. Unknown URLs are not inferred and console output is not labelled empty.

The exact synthetic blob was retried successfully. A different original-QA tree batch containing real device/archive metadata was denied by automatic approval review; that action remains stopped. Read-only public identity verification still reports 3.13, with no claimed remote branch or deployment change.

compoundRigidContact.readOnlyGeometryConclusion: At the positive sampled poses the four vehicle boxes remain about 0.30 m above y=0; front wheel bump-stop cylinders slightly cross the ground plane. Ground is the only nearby static AABB candidate. This supports wheel hard-stop contact as an inference, not a captured Cannon pair.

visualReview.observed: Chase view shows the car, the lower Weave road, overhead structure and sky. The navigation displays the first left turn and 960 m remaining. Recording, four-wheel support and bench supply are visible; the mounted experimental rear assemblies are visible.
visualReview.limits: A single start image is not video and is not an atomic same-frame telemetry bundle. Software-renderer preview frame rate is not hardware performance.

limitations: One original route from the legal city spawn, using real native keys and the existing physics. The external key chooser is QA operation, not human handling evaluation.

Lower Foundry entrance reached within the existing 8 m arrival radius; the vehicle did not need to touch the exact center coordinate. Upper-road ascent, maintenance court and the full drive-flight challenge remain untested by this run.
This x=100 northbound drive does not prove the separate transverse X crossing at z=-100. Its existing geometry-ray evidence is separate.
Existing bench supply, no wind, clear day and dry road. No flight thrust was requested; 0 kg gas throughput does not establish finite-air flight performance.
Native key receipts are complete in the original application journal; eight external returned lines and one collector telemetry-count difference are explicitly unresolved.
Geometry analysis does not replace unrecorded contact pair/force data, and the route is not described as compound-contact-free.
The two PNGs are original start/end stills, not a full route video. No RGB pixel edits or exposure postprocessing were performed.

numericalBoundaries.energyScope: Translation, body/wheel rotation, gravity and suspension spring potential. The stored spring compression is the last force-evaluation value. No drive/regen input in these declared passive fixtures. Energy screens are not a complete deformable tyre, restitution or damage validation.
limits: Neither severe fixture has a converged complete impact trajectory. Agreement at 60/120/240 Hz caller intervals alone was a false impression and is explicitly contradicted by finer references.
The 120 Hz product input interval is retained; hard contact can use the same solver at 960 Hz internally. This is not a claim of three pure 60/120/240 Hz solvers agreeing.

The continuous crowned support envelope is a radius-R sphere clipped to the existing finite tyre width, not a measured tyre profile; independent 20-sided rigid wheel stops retain their facets. Tyre deformation, rim damage and suspension structural failure are outside this model.
Full-width finite response and lower penetration do not establish that a real car could safely cross a 10 cm curb at 90 km/h.
Both 90 km/h 10 cm fixtures retain unresolved post-impact trajectory convergence. This is an open physical/numerical limitation, not reclassified as normal or accepted.
numericalBoundaries.scope: Neither mechanical-energy screening nor smaller contact-depth/SAT peaks closes complete collision energy accounting or complete severe-step trajectory convergence. Finite recovery means original-task cancellation plus recovery landing, not original-task success.
